accepted_concepts.summary: Adaptive music must be expressed as event-driven musical states with declared intensity, priority, fallback, channel ownership and coexistence with critical SFX.
Horizontal resequencing is useful only when translated into BPM, time signature, NTSC/PAL frame timing, allowed transition points, stinger/bridge ids and missed-window fallback.
Loop and tail handling are accepted as asset/export requirements captured by seamless_loop_report; they do not imply runtime reverb or middleware features.
SFX and timbres must declare gameplay role before timbre: alert, damage, confirmation, threat, reward, ambience, UI, boss cue, transition or intentional silence.

rejected_or_not_absorbed.claim: FMOD/Wwise/RTPC behavior maps directly to Mega Drive audio
rejected_or_not_absorbed.reason: Rejected. Middleware concepts must be translated into discrete states, fades, stingers, pre-rendered variants or a custom-driver handoff.

rejected_or_not_absorbed.claim: Low-pass filters and continuous parameter automation are default Mega Drive capabilities
rejected_or_not_absorbed.reason: Rejected unless a project-specific driver, asset variant or hardware-feasible substitute is documented and validated.

rejected_or_not_absorbed.claim: The example C code is canonical SGDK/XGM2 architecture
rejected_or_not_absorbed.reason: Rejected. The snippet is illustrative, contains non-validated driver calls and mixes input/debug/UI patterns owned by other skills.

rejected_or_not_absorbed.claim: A music theory transcript proves excellent or AAA audio
rejected_or_not_absorbed.reason: Rejected. E1_text can improve candidate rules, but production still requires contracts, assets, auditory test, build and emulator evidence.

required_followups_before_production: bar_beat_transition_plan or equivalent documented timing plan
validate_audio report when audio resources exist
BlastEm evidence when a ROM delivery claims runtime audio
